items.title: A cache that stores how an AI reasoned, not just what it said
items.why: Lets a tiny model replay a big model's solved reasoning as code, cutting repeat costs 16-291x once it's learned a problem type.

items.title: A classic coding-interview proof turns out to be wrong but still true
items.why: The 'small-to-large merging' trick everyone cites had a shaky proof; a GitHub fix replaces it with one that actually holds up.

items.title: A German toilet-queue game crashes real microcontrollers for fun
items.why: Every knock on a virtual festival-toilet door overloads a real ESP8266 until it crashes - a playful lesson in resource-exhaustion attacks.

items.title: Open-source boards turn any HDMI feed into a Pi camera input
items.why: WarpKVM's RK628 boards convert HDMI into CSI at 4K30, so a Pi or CM4 can treat any HDMI source like a plug-in camera.

items.title: A Windows zero-day turns a logging feature into SYSTEM access
items.why: SignDrop abuses CLFS recovery-file creation via symlink redirection to hand a standard user a SYSTEM-owned file - no patch yet.

items.title: Relabel interview nerves as excitement, not calm, before you walk in
items.why: A well-replicated trick: say 'I'm excited' instead of 'calm down' - it measurably improves performance under pressure.
items.source: Journal of Experimental Psychology: General (Alison Wood Brooks, Harvard)

items.title: Deep-sleep brain waves that travel less may flag early memory risk
items.why: Berkeley: tau buildup weakens coordinated slow waves in deep sleep, tracking with worse next-day recall - protect your sleep depth.

items.title: In a 10,000-student study, how often you exercise beat how hard
items.why: Norwegian cohort of 10,460: how often you exercised predicted anxiety/depression risk better than how hard or how long.

items.title: Your mmap succeeded but SIGBUS'd anyway? Check these four things
items.why: A HugeTLB mmap only reserves space; faults need backing. Check smaps' ht flag, file size, hugepage pool, and your cgroup's hugetlb limits.

items.title: IIT Mandi turns material defects into brain-like memory chips
items.why: Cracks and sulphur gaps in a WS2 flake let one device switch two ways, mimicking both synapse and neuron behaviour for brain-like chips.

drill.q: Which claim in item 8 is the weakest?
options: "how often you exercise beat how hard" - frequency winning over intensity
"predicted anxiety/depression risk a year later" - a before-and-after prospective measurement
drill.why: The underlying research gives no effect sizes, so 'beat' overstates what was really just a more consistent association for frequency, not a quantified head-to-head result - and the observational design still can't prove intensity matters less.
